modules.label: Prompt Registry
modules.purpose: Holds the record of every prompt property — purpose, owner, model name, access level, status, tags — and the immutable chain of revisions behind it, so a teammate can find the prompt, see who owns it, and read what changed between two revisions, and so the gateway can resolve a model name to exactly one released revision.

modules.label: Evaluation
modules.purpose: Holds each prompt property's fixed suites of 10-20 hand-authored cases, runs them against a candidate revision and against the currently released one, and reports per-case pass/fail plus the token and money delta — so a reviewer decides on measured evidence instead of reading a diff and guessing.

inputs.label: author a suite, start a run, open the comparison

modules.label: Release Control
modules.purpose: Carries a revision from submitted, through a recorded human decision, to released — and back again on a restore or a withdrawal. It composes the evidence a reviewer needs onto one screen, records the decision, and issues the single command that moves the released pointer.

inputs.label: submit, request a restore, request a withdrawal
inputs.from: Prompt Owner via the web SPA

inputs.label: review, approve, release, break-glass, close a task
inputs.from: Reviewer / Approver via the web SPA

outputs.label: 8 history events, in the same transaction

modules.label: Gateway
modules.purpose: Serves an OpenAI-compatible endpoint where the model field names a prompt property, resolves it to the released revision, composes the call, dispatches it through provider-access, and returns the response — or the revision's fallback answer when the upstream fails — while every call is recorded off the response path with the version ID that served it.

inputs.label: chat completions and model list, by model name

modules.label: Provider Access
modules.purpose: Holds each workspace's own provider configurations and credentials, and is the single place in Prope that makes an upstream model call. Live gateway traffic and batch eval runs are both issued here, with a credential that never leaves this process.

inputs.label: configuration, credential, rotation, verification
inputs.from: Workspace Admin via the web SPA

outputs.label: chat completions and model list — Prope's only egress

modules.label: Call Ledger
modules.purpose: Accepts every completed call off the response path, persists its metadata durably and its bodies best-effort, prices its token usage against an effective-dated price table, and answers the one question those totals decide: has this workspace hit its spend ceiling. It is a sink — it calls nothing.

inputs.label: enqueue(call_record), after the response is flushed
price rows, spend ceilings, retention window
inputs.from: Workspace Admin via the web SPA

modules.label: Access Control
modules.purpose: Authenticates every actor — a person with a session, or a consuming product with an API key — and answers every may-this-actor-do-this question in the system, so no other module holds a copy of the rules. It is the oracle six modules consult and it calls none of its callers.

outputs.label: 10 history events, in the same transaction

modules.label: Property History
modules.purpose: Holds the append-only record of every state change in Prope — actor, action, target, timestamp, reason — in one table with one schema, written through one writer, so that who changed this, when, and why has a single answer. It depends on nothing, which is what lets access-control depend on it.

externals.label: Web SPA (prope-web)
externals.purpose: The management surface, served same-origin by Caddy. It calls six modules' /api/v1 routes directly with a session cookie.

externals.label: Consuming product's OpenAI SDK
externals.purpose: Outside this repository and outside this team. It calls /v1 with a consumer API key and OpenAI's own wire format.

externals.label: The workspace's upstream provider
externals.purpose: Bring-your-own-key. Prope holds no provider account. This is the only outbound internet egress in the system.
